svg.text: Longest Consecutive Sequence — only true starts extend a chain nums = [100,4,200,1,3,2]
Put every value into a set. For each value num, only start extending if num−1 is NOT in the set —
that is what guarantees num is the FIRST element of its run, so each run is only ever walked once.

g.text: num=100: 99 not in set → start! chain: 100 → len 1
num=4: 3 IS in set → skip (not a true start)
num=200: 199 not in set → start! chain: 200 → len 1
num=1: 0 not in set → start! chain: 1,2,3,4 → len 4 ← longest
num=3, num=2: their (num−1) ARE in the set → skip both

svg.text: Why this is O(n) overall, not O(n²)
Every value is visited by the inner while loop at most once across the ENTIRE run of the algorithm —
once a value has been consumed as part of some chain, it can never be revisited by another chain.
So the total work done by all the inner loops added together is bounded by n, giving amortised O(n).
